title: Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship 2027
aboutScholarship:
The Griffith University Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship is a merit-based scholarship designed to recognise and support outstanding international students commencing undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degrees at Griffith University in Australia.

The scholarship aims to attract academically strong students from around the world by reducing the cost of tuition fees and helping them access quality higher education. Successful applicants receive a tuition fee reduction of 50% for the normal duration of their eligible degree, provided they continue to meet the scholarship's academic and enrolment requirements.

Griffith University offers a wide range of study options across areas such as business, engineering, information technology, health, science, law, education, arts, and social sciences. Applicants should check their chosen programme's eligibility before applying.

 

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Applicants must be citizens of a country other than Australia or New Zealand.
  • Applicants must be new, commencing international students who have received a conditional or unconditional offer to study at Griffith University by the relevant scholarship deadline.
  • Applicants must have a minimum GPA of 6.0 on a 7.0-point scale, or an equivalent academic result.
  • Applicants must meet the academic and English-language entry requirements for their chosen programme.
  • Applicants must enrol full-time in an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree commencing in 2026 or 2027.
  • Applicants must submit the scholarship application with the required academic documents and a personal statement.
  • Higher Degree Research programmes, online programmes, Study Abroad programmes, diploma programmes, MBA programmes, English-language programmes, and certain other courses are excluded.

 

Benefits:

  • Covers 50% of eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework tuition fees.
  • The scholarship applies for the normal duration of the degree, subject to meeting the university's ongoing eligibility requirements.
  • Reduces the tuition fee burden for international students studying at Griffith University.
  • Provides an opportunity to study at an Australian university with access to academic resources, student support services, and industry connections.

 

Eligible Courses and Exclusions

The scholarship applies to eligible undergraduate and postgraduate coursework degrees at Griffith University. However, some programmes are excluded, including Higher Degree Research programmes, online programmes, Study Abroad programmes, diploma programmes, the MBA, English-language courses, and programmes offered only part-time or in partnership with another organisation.

Applicants should check the complete exclusions on the official scholarship page before applying.

 

Documents Required

Applicants should prepare the following documents:

  • Academic certificates and transcripts for completed qualifications, provided as certified copies where required.
  • A conditional or unconditional offer letter from Griffith University.
  • A personal statement of 250–500 words explaining why the applicant is applying, why they selected their programme at Griffith, and how they intend to make an impact in the future.
  • Supporting evidence of academic achievements or other relevant accomplishments, where applicable.
  • Any additional documents requested by the university or scholarship application form.

 

Application Deadline:

  • Trimester 1, 2027: 28 November 2026
  • Trimester 2, 2027: 10 April 2027
  • Students completing Australian Year 12 have a separate deadline of 2 January 2027 for Trimester 1, 2027.

 

Official Website / Apply Link:

  • Scholarship details: https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/scholarships-finance/scholarships/vice-chancellors-international-scholarship
  • Direct scholarship application: https://www.griffith.edu.au/international/scholarships-finance/scholarships/application
  • International admission application: https://www.griffith.edu.au/apply/international

 

How to Apply

  1. Visit the official Griffith University international admissions page: https://www.griffith.edu.au/apply/international
  2. Choose an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework programme and review its academic and English-language entry requirements.
  3. Submit an application for admission to Griffith University.
  4. Obtain a conditional or unconditional offer for the selected programme.
  5. Visit the official Vice Chancellor’s International Scholarship page and review the relevant intake deadline.
  6. Complete the scholarship application form, attach the required certified academic records, and submit the personal statement.
  7. Submit the application before the deadline for the intended intake and monitor communications from Griffith University regarding the outcome.

title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Scholarship 2027

The programme provides students with an opportunity to gain international academic exposure, develop cross-cultural competencies, and benefit from diverse teaching and research environments.

Selected students can study at two or more universities in different countries as part of an integrated master's programme. Depending on the selected course and scholarship award, financial support may cover participation costs, travel, visa expenses, and a living allowance. The programme offers opportunities across a wide range of academic disciplines, including engineering, environmental sciences, public health, data science, economics, social sciences, and other specialised fields.

  2. Identify a programme matching your academic background and career interests.

title: Central Sector Scheme of Scholarship for College and University Students

Every year, 82,000 scholarships are awarded under this scheme, equally distributed between 41,000 boys and 41,000 girls.

Applicants must meet the following conditions:

  • Must have scored above the 80th percentile in Class 12 from a recognized board
  • Annual family income should be less than ₹8 lakh

  • Should not be receiving any other scholarship or fee reimbursement
  • Diploma students are not eligible

  • Age limit: 18 to 25 years

  • SC: 15%
  • ST: 7.5%
  • OBC: 27%

  • ₹20,000 per year for postgraduate studies

title: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships 2027–2028
aboutScholarship:
The Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are prestigious international scholarships offered by the Swiss Confederation to promote academic exchange, international research collaboration, and scientific cooperation. Administered by the Federal Commission for Scholarships for Foreign Students (FCS/ESKAS), the programme supports talented researchers and selected artists from eligible countries who wish to pursue advanced research or doctoral studies in Switzerland.

The scholarships provide opportunities to work with experienced academics and research teams at recognised Swiss universities, federal institutes of technology, universities of applied sciences, and eligible research institutes. The programme primarily supports postgraduate research and PhD studies rather than ordinary bachelor's or taught master's degree programmes.

1. Research Fellowships

Research fellowships support early-career researchers, including doctoral candidates pursuing a PhD in their home country, who wish to undertake a research project at a Swiss higher education institution or recognised research institute.

The fellowship lasts between 6 and 12 months, with no extension available. Applicants must have a master's degree or equivalent, a detailed research plan, and support from a qualified academic supervisor in Switzerland.

2. PhD Scholarships

PhD scholarships support eligible candidates who wish to pursue doctoral studies at a Swiss university or recognised research institution. Funding is provided for an initial 12-month period and may be renewed twice, up to a maximum of 36 months, subject to satisfactory academic progress and the programme's conditions.

Applicants must identify a suitable Swiss academic supervisor and provide a research proposal. Candidates applying to a doctoral school may also need an official admission confirmation, depending on the programme structure.

 

Eligibility Criteria:

  • Applicants must be eligible citizens of a participating country. Indian applicants should check the India-specific scholarship categories and requirements.
  • Applicants must generally have been born after 31 December 1991 for the 2027–2028 cycle.
  • A master's degree or equivalent must be completed by 31 July 2027. For ETH Zurich, the deadline is 30 June 2027.
  • Applicants must prepare a detailed research proposal with a timeline and clearly defined objectives.
  • A letter of support from an academic supervisor at an eligible Swiss higher education institution is mandatory.
  • Applicants must demonstrate strong academic credentials, research ability, motivation, and potential for future research collaboration.
  • The research must be undertaken full-time in Switzerland.
  • Applicants must comply with country-specific eligibility rules, application procedures, and the relevant scholarship category's conditions.

 

Benefits:

  • Monthly scholarship of CHF 2,450 to support basic living expenses.
  • One-time housing allowance of CHF 600.
  • Compulsory health insurance premiums covered for eligible scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries.
  • Half-Fare Travelcard for public transportation in Switzerland.
  • Return-flight allowance for eligible scholarship holders from non-EU/EFTA countries.
  • Research fellowship duration of 6–12 months.
  • PhD scholarship support for up to 36 months, subject to satisfactory academic progress and renewal conditions.
  • Access to research facilities and academic supervision at eligible Swiss institutions.

Important: The scholarship does not cover tuition or semester fees, conference participation, or research fieldwork expenses. These costs may have to be paid by the scholarship holder.

 

Documents Required

Applicants should prepare the following documents, as applicable to their selected category:

  • Updated curriculum vitae, including academic qualifications, research experience, publications, awards, and relevant professional experience.
  • Letter of motivation explaining the purpose of the proposed stay in Switzerland and future academic or career plans.
  • Detailed research proposal with a timeline and milestones, using the required FCS/ESKAS format.
  • Letter of support from the Swiss academic supervisor, accompanied by the supervisor's short CV.
  • Academic certificates and university transcripts, with certified translations where required.
  • Passport copy.
  • Contact details for two academic referees who may be asked to submit recommendation letters through the application system.
  • Additional documents required by the selected university, doctoral school, or scholarship category.

Applicants should consult the official checklist because requirements differ between research fellowships and PhD scholarships.

title: SDEF India Scholarship 2026–27

The SDEF India Scholarship Program 2026–27, offered by the Swami Dayanand Education Foundation (SDEF), supports academically deserving students from financially constrained families who are pursuing full-time undergraduate professional education in India. The scholarship is available to students entering the first year of an eligible professional undergraduate programme for the 2026–27 academic year. Selection is based on academic merit, financial need, family circumstances, authenticity of the application, and performance in subsequent selection stages.

 

Eligible Courses

The scholarship is available for eligible full-time undergraduate professional programmes, including:

  • Engineering & Technology: B.Tech./B.E.
  • Medicine: MBBS
  • Dentistry: BDS
  • Nursing: B.Sc. Nursing/B.Nursing
  • Pharmacy: B.Pharm./Pharm.D
  • Architecture: B.Arch.
  • Veterinary Science: BVSc & AH
  • Other eligible professional undergraduate programmes may also be considered where the applicant has qualified in the relevant recognised entrance examination.

 

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must meet all of the following requirements:

  • Must be enrolled in the first year of a full-time undergraduate professional programme in India for the 2026–27 academic year.
  • Must be pursuing one of the eligible professional programmes.
  • Must have secured at least 80% marks or equivalent CGPA in Class XII.
  • Must meet the applicable entrance examination requirement, wherever required.
  • For applicable courses, candidates must have the required entrance examination qualification, such as:
    • JEE Main: AIR 50,000 or below
    • JEE Advanced: AIR 40,000 or below
    • NEET UG: AIR 50,000 or below
    • NATA: Minimum 100 marks
  • Annual family income from all sources must be ₹12 lakh or less.
  • Applicants must provide complete, accurate and verifiable information and supporting documents.
  • Shortlisted candidates must be willing to participate in the aptitude assessment, document verification, interview and other selection stages, as applicable.

 

Not Eligible

  • Students studying in the second year or later.
  • Students enrolled in part-time undergraduate programmes.
  • Students who have taken a drop/gap year after Class XII.
  • Applicants who do not meet the required academic, income or entrance examination criteria.

 

Scholarship Benefits

  • Scholarship amount of up to ₹50,000 per academic year.
  • Total scholarship value can be up to ₹2,00,000 over four academic years.
  • The scholarship is renewable annually, subject to continued eligibility and satisfactory academic performance.
  • Scholarship funds are disbursed directly to the student's college or university account and are used towards approved educational expenses.
  • Funds are not disbursed directly into the student's personal bank account.

 

Required Documents

Applicants are required to upload the following documents:

  • Recent passport-size photograph
  • Aadhaar Card
  • Class X marksheet
  • Class XII marksheet
  • Relevant entrance examination scorecard
  • Admission letter
  • College ID
  • Latest college fee receipt
  • Family income proof
  • Electricity, water or gas utility bill
  • Three photographs of the applicant's residence

Additional documents may be required, where applicable:

  • Agricultural land documents
  • Educational loan documents
  • ITR
  • Salary slip/salary certificate
  • Pension proof
  • Other documents requested by SDEF

 

Selection Process

The selection process may include:

  1. Online application submission
  2. Initial screening based on eligibility and academic performance
  3. Verification of submitted documents and financial information
  4. Aptitude assessment for shortlisted applicants
